question: For a representative stop-level acoustic-activation regression, how much does treating ten route stops as conditionally independent change uncertainty relative to clustering repeated stop outcomes within species x route-night?
population: Exactly the 2,835 weather-eligible strictly-prior-history matched pairs used in the rain-amount and residual-dependence diagnostics.
risk_set: Species x stop cells with CallingIndex=0 / no recorded call in the drier route-run; response is binary calling-positive status at the same StopNumber in the wetter run.

model.formula: wet_activation ~ rain_contrast + temp_difference + doy_difference + year_gap + C(State) + C(RunNumber) + C(species)
model.same_point_estimate_rule: Fit this formula once; compare covariance estimators without changing coefficients or the analysis sample.

covariance_estimators.iid_primary_reference: Model-based GLM covariance treating cells as independent.
covariance_estimators.species_route_night_primary: Sandwich covariance clustered by focal pair x species, so the up-to-ten stop cells for the same species and route-night form one cluster.
covariance_estimators.route_pair_secondary: Sandwich covariance clustered by focal matched pair, allowing dependence across all taxa and stops within the route-night contrast.

primary_output: species-route-night cluster standard error and 95% CI
route-pair clustered SE as a broader-dependence sensitivity

interpretation.se_inflation: If clustered SE exceeds IID SE, treating stops as independent understates uncertainty for this representative activation regression.
interpretation.no_inflation: Do not claim general underestimation of uncertainty if clustered SE is not larger.
interpretation.boundary: This is not a reanalysis of a specific published occupancy-trend estimator and does not establish the exact bias or design effect of such models.

provenance: Post-hoc diagnostic after the explicit 2026-10-03 reopening; not independent confirmation.
